title: Memory Work
address: 250 Fort York Blvd, Toronto, ON M5V 3K9
description: Situated at the western entrance to The Bentway, Memory Work is a mural made up of twelve embellished photographic portraits of revolutionary women and non-binary figures from a future Toronto. Initiated by studio From Later with artist Rajni Perera and Memory Work Collective, this speculative monument imagines a city characterized by collective care and politics that value nurturing over growth.

title: Declaration of the Understory
address: 250 Fort York Blvd, Toronto, ON M5V 3K9
description: Secwépemc artist Tania Willard approaches the space below the highway as a tree canopy, reminiscent of the “understory” floor of southern Ontario forests, where pockets of shade and sunlight shape unique ecosystems below. In a stunning mixed-media installation, floral motifs, iridescence, and powerful slogans offer a mediation on the power of shade as a lifeforce.

title: Bathed in Strange Light
address: 250 Fort York Blvd, Toronto, ON M5V 3K9
description: Working in collaboration with the sun’s rhythms, Natalie Hunter’s photographs on the windows of The Bentway Studio (facing Canoe Landing Park) explore how ever-shifting sunlight shapes our experience of public spaces. As the sun moves throughout the day, translucent images cast down a colorful, slow-moving cinema.

title: Petal to Paper: Paper Magnolia Workshop
description: Join us to create lifelike paper magnolia with botanical accuracy!Join paper artist Nancy Lalicon for the "Paper to Petal: Paper Magnolia Workshop." In this 4-hour session, participants will learn to create lifelike Magnolias with their leathery, two coloured leaves. Magnolia flowers come in shades of white, pink, purple and hints of yellow. Nancy will guide you through constructing the flowers in the colours of your choice by using templates for the petals and leaves. You will have the opportunity to use coloured media to enhance their beauty. Discover the art of paper floristry and leave with your own stunning creations.Materials Provided:Selection of doublette crepe paper180g green crepe paperFloral WireFloral TapeAleenes GlueSoft Pastels including PanPastelsAlcohol MarkersVarious brushes and spongesKraft paper for wrapping flowersWhat To Bring:Sharp scissors (4”-5”) (optional)Additional colouring materials (optional)Saturday, January 31 from 10:00 AM- 2:30 PM. There will be a 30-minute break for lunch. We recommend bringing a lunch as there are limited options nearby.Registration: Public $67, TBG Members $57 (plus applicable taxes and fees)About Nancy LaliconNancy Lalicon is a multi-media sculptor specialized in making botanically accurate paper flowers and plants, and in facilitating workshops for for community art organizations and local groups around Toronto and the GTA. From Peonies to Jupiters Beard to the Blazing Star, Nancy has mastered the intricate art of creating environmentally friendly paper replicas; a modern day, three dimensional take on botanical drawing.Trained in the Fine Arts at the University of Victoria and the Emily Carr College of Art in BC, she received an MFA from Concordia University, Montreal. Nancy lives in East Toronto with a large family who lovingly tolerate all her studio hours and mountains of flowers and roots.Join Toronto Botanical GardenJoin the Toronto Botanical Garden (TBG) as a member to get a discount on this program, upcoming events and classes, and free parking. description: Swan Lake is a natural Kettle Lake. When the ice blocks melt, kettle holes are left in the sandur. Kettle holes can also occur in ridge shaped deposits of loose rock fragments called till.
